claims.text: An architecture decision record is a short document about one decision: a title, a status, the context that called for it, the decision itself and its consequences.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 1; content/glossary.yaml architecture-decision-record short_en; docs/adr/README.md @ stage-3 lines 3-5; docs/adr/template.md

claims.text: At stage-3 Đơn Hàng keeps ADRs as numbered files in docs/adr/, and docs/adr/README.md lists ten of them, 0001 to 0010, each with title and status; README lines 3-5 say an ADR sits beside the code so it is reviewed and versioned with it.

ADR 0003 lines 1-6: title splits Payments into a service linked by a saga; status Đã chấp nhận; decided by the team lead; no comment deadline as it was written after the work. A comment deadline is the date by which the team may comment on a proposed ADR (README step 2).

ADR 0003 lines 8-9 say it was written after the fact, following ADR 0001 (which chose docs/adr/ and had earlier decisions rewritten as ADRs), and point to docs/design/refund-design.md (bản 2) for the step-by-step refund flow; the ADR records only the decision.

ADR 0003 context (lines 11-17): refunds must meet YC-7, YC-9 and YC-10; the gateway key and money records are the most sensitive part; in design version 1 every copy of DonHang.Api held that key and could read and write the payments table.
ADR 0003 lines 19-28 hold the options; lines 32-36 choose a separate service linked by a saga and give why two-phase commit and keeping refunds in the API were rejected.

ADR 0003 consequences (lines 40-47): order and refund agree only after a while; one more service to run; each step must be safely repeatable since a message can arrive twice; failures compensated by a reverse step, not rollback; old payments table stays in donhang as debt N2, pointing to ADR 0008.
refund-design.md at stage-3 is version 2 (bản 2); version 1 kept everything in DonHang.Api; its last lines say the file is edited in the same pull request as the code when the plan changes.

A design doc describes how to build one thing and is updated as the plan changes; an accepted ADR keeps one decision's reasons as they were when made, and points to the design doc instead of repeating it.
When a decision changes, a new ADR records the new decision rather than the accepted one being rewritten.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/README.md @ stage-3 lines 43-45; outline of management.l3.superseding-an-adr

claims.text: An ADR is worth writing when a decision is costly to reverse or people will later ask why it was made; a choice that is easy to undo, such as a variable name, needs no record.
ADR 0001 weighed a shared wiki page for all decisions and rejected it because it is not reviewed through pull requests like code and gets edited until nobody knows what the decision first rested on.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docs/adr/0001-ghi-quyet-dinh-bang-adr.md, Các phương án (wiki bullet)

claims.text: Each ADR costs writing and review time; a record list full of small choices hides the decisions that matter.
claims.source_hint: Outline misconception 2; docs/adr/0001 Hệ quả first bullet

claims.text: The refund flow's first retry after a gateway failure waits 1 minute (then 2, 4, 8 minutes, at most 1 hour apart, within 24 hours).
At stage-3 every service that sends or receives messages (DonHang.Api, Notifications, Payments) uses RabbitMQ through outbox and inbox, so replacing the broker is costly to reverse.
